newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Tuesday on continued weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,300 yuan ($2,444) per tonne, down 120 yuan. It opened at 20,350 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,360 and a low of 20,260.

September fell 20 to 21,180 yuan, October 120 to 20,650, November 70 to 20,430, December 120 to 20,320, the February 1997 contract 120 to 20,300, March 150 to 20,330, April 800 to 20,400 and May 560 to 20,450.
Combined volume rose to 40,730 tonnes from 21,090.
Copper opened down and moved in a narrow range at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said that overnight losses on the London Metals Exchange depressed confidence of long position holders in Shanghai and long liquidation pushed prices down further.
"Long liquidation by retail investors because of weak sentiment was responsible for today's falls but it was not panic because there was no especially bad news," one trader said.
Traders said that copper will find strong support at the 20,000-yuan level in the short term on positive fundamentals and technical factors.
"Short position holders will take profits around 20,000 yuan because most believe it will not breach that level, unless copper breaches $1,929 on the LME," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move in a range of 20,000 and 20,500 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. September fell 20 to 14,160 yuan, October 10 to 14,260 and November 50 to 14,270.
Combined volume fell to 460 tonnes from 610.
